<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6e8e38a638b360c3b53307fe5f68e491f215b173` — the merge of head `e8b22f7fdf0add5fc29513625eeed3a7f7138578` into base `316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6e8e38a638b360c3b53307fe5f68e491f215b173 && git checkout 6e8e38a638b360c3b53307fe5f68e491f215b173
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e e8b22f7fdf0add5fc29513625eeed3a7f7138578 && git checkout -B drift-repro 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e && git merge --no-ff e8b22f7fdf0add5fc29513625eeed3a7f7138578

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Shape:** open, draft, base `main`; first line `Fixes #35307`, and the PR delivers the whole card (the card's only ask is the hit title); no closing keyword near another card (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36523`, all rows ok).
- **Premise:** held (claim 7082444246). The dev corrected one PM assumption in the report (7083127305): `recipient_type` values are user / group / position / unit_and_subordinates, there is no `role` kind. Accepted; it narrows nothing the card asked.
- **Scope:** 3 files, all on the claim's file surface: `protocol-record-reads.ts` (+90/-1), a new card-named test file, one changeset. `sys-record-share.object.ts` and `packages/spec/src/**` untouched. Not governed (`check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36523`: 0 of 3 paths), 389 changed lines.
- **Diff read:** the recipient pointer is recognised by the declaration the console face reads (`type: text`, `widget: 'recipient-picker'`, `dependsOn` naming `recipient_type`), not by object name; only when the pointer is not reference-typed (`!titleTarget`), so the #35292 follow is untouched. Ids are grouped per directory and each directory is read once through the existing `readReferenceTitles`, so the searcher, the gates (`canServeApiOperation`, `canReadObject`) and the dispositions are the reference follow's. A row whose kind is unreadable or has no directory pays no read and keeps the stored value.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/35307-search-recipient-title.md`, read sentence by sentence against the diff: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch; the kind→directory list (user→`sys_user`, team→`sys_team`, business_unit / unit_and_subordinates→`sys_business_unit`), "read once per swept object, as the searcher", "a directory read that fails fails the search", "group or position keeps its stored value" and "`record` still carries the stored id" each match the code.

Ablation reported 5 red / 7 green with the call site reverted. The existing #35292 test files are unchanged. Check-runs at this head: 39 success, 18 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`. Local gate ledger: `/mnt/project-files/objectstack-seat2/35307-gates-ran.txt` (67 families, 0 NOT-MEASURED).
- **Accepted deviations:** (1) the dispatch suggested "a failing directory read keeps the hit with the bare id"; the dev kept the #34175 disposition (a non-refusal failure fails the search), which is what the 2026-08-29 search ruling and the pinned #35292 tests require; the PM suggestion was wrong, the PR is right. (2) Maintainer brief has four lines (os-dev.md), not six. (3) New test file instead of extending `search-title-lookup.test.ts` (claim surface).
- **Out of scope:** the kind→directory table now lives twice (console `RECIPIENT_RECORD_KINDS`, server `RECIPIENT_DIRECTORY_OBJECTS`), each naming the other — Acceptance notes, not filed: no defect today and zero pull for a spec-owned table. `group` recipients have no directory object on either side and no producer writes them — Acceptance notes, not filed (zero pull). `position` titles via the registry — dropped: no producer writes a non-user row.
- **Landing:** non-governed, ≤3000 lines, K = 1 (`landing-k.mjs`: ok) ⇒ area lands it in this stroke (ready + auto-merge).
